question: Explain overfitting, compare L2 regularization and early stopping, then summarize their advantages.
answer: Overfitting occurs when a model performs exceptionally well on the training data but poorly on unseen validation or test data, indicating it has memorized noise rather than learned generalizable patterns. [S6] It requires a validation set and is sensitive to patience value. [S6] L2 regularization and early stopping are complementary, often used together. [S6] L2 regularization is smoother and more reproducible, early stopping cheaper. [S3]

3. Early stopping Early stopping monitors validation loss during training and stops when it has not
improved for a fixed number of epochs (the patience); the best checkpoint is restored. Advantages:
it needs no change to the model, saves training compute, and the stopping epoch acts as an
implicit regularizer. Disadvantages: it requires a held-out validation set that is then not used for
training, results are sensitive to the patience value, and noisy validation curves can trigger a
premature stop. 4. Dropout Dropout randomly zeroes a fraction p of hidden units at each training
step so units cannot co-adapt. It is applied only during training. It is mainly used for neural
networks.

What overfitting means in practice A model overfits when its training accuracy is far higher than its validation accuracy. The gap between the two (train accuracy minus validation accuracy) is the simplest warning sign. 2. L2 regularization (weight decay) L2 regularization adds a penalty proportional to the sum of squared weights to the loss, which shrinks weights toward zero without usually making them exactly zero. Advantages: it is smooth, works with gradient-based optimizers, and keeps all features. S2.title: Ml Lecture Notes
S2.text: 3. Generalization, Overfitting and the Bias-Variance Tradeoff A model generalizes when it performs well on new data, not just on the data used for training. Overfitting happens when a model memorizes noise and idiosyncrasies of the training set: training error is very low but validation or test error is much higher. Underfitting happens when the model is too simple to capture the pattern, so both training and validation error are high. The bias-variance tradeoff explains this. Bias is the error caused by overly simple assumptions; high-bias models underfit. Variance is the sensitivity of a model to the particular training sample; high-variance models overfit. Total expected error is bias squared plus variance plus irreducible noise. Increasing model complexity lowers bias but raises variance.

S4.title: Ml Exercise Guide
S4.text:
Assignment 1: Diagnosing a Model
Task. You trained a decision tree classifier and obtained 99% training accuracy but 71% validation accuracy. Explain what is happening and propose two fixes.
Expected answer. The large gap between training and validation accuracy is the signature of overfitting (high variance). Fixes include limiting the maximum depth of the tree, requiring a minimum number of samples per leaf, pruning, switching to a random forest, or collecting more data. Report validation performance using cross-validation rather than a single split.

S5.title: Ml Model Diagnostics Handbook
S5.text:
3. Regularization Strength in scikit-learn
In scikit-learn LogisticRegression the parameter C is the inverse of the regularization strength: a
smaller C means stronger regularization, and the default is C=1.0. For Ridge regression the
parameter alpha works the opposite way: a larger alpha means stronger shrinkage.
L2 regularization (ridge) shrinks all weights toward zero; L1 regularization (lasso) can set some
weights exactly to zero and therefore performs feature selection.
